item.mechanism: The presence of Ti atoms induces an antiferromagnetic coupling with Fe, Co, and Ni atoms, which reduces the overall saturation magnetization (Ms) and contributes to the high coercive field in the fcc phase.
item.operating_conditions: Electronic structure calculations at 0 K; theoretical ground state analysis
item.supporting_observation: Electronic structure calculations show the Ti magnetic moment is antiparallel to Fe, Co, and Ni, and the total moment is lower than in FeCoNi without Ti.
item.scope_limits: This mechanism explains the reduction in Ms but is not the direct cause of high Hc; the high Hc is attributed to the resulting low Ms via anisotropy, not the coupling itself directly.
item.alternatives_considered: Direct orbital moment enhancement was considered but rejected as the orbital moments in FeCoNiTi are smaller than in FeCoNi.
quotes: In both phases, the magnetic moments of Fe, Co, and Ni exhibit ferromagnetic alignment, while the orientation of the Ti moment is antiparallel to that of Fe, Co, or Ni.

item.mechanism: The fcc phase exhibits a ferromagnetic ground state due to the disparate energy dependence of the total density of states (DOS) between spin-up and spin-down electrons at the Fermi energy.
item.operating_conditions: Electronic structure calculations (0 K theoretical ground state)
item.supporting_observation: The calculated total DOS shows a clear difference between spin-up and spin-down configurations at the Fermi level, confirming ferromagnetism.
item.scope_limits: This is a theoretical prediction of the ground state; experimental Ms values are lower than theoretical values, indicating the presence of spin-canted components not captured by the simple parallel spin model.
item.alternatives_considered: Paramagnetic or antiferromagnetic ground states were implicitly considered but ruled out by the DOS asymmetry.
quotes: Electronic structure calculations were executed to elucidate the ferromagnetic characteristics inherent in each phase, and the outcomes are delineated in Figure 4 a–f.
The band calculation treats the FM state with spins of Fe, Co, and Ni aligning in parallel, while the Ti spin aligns antiparallel.

item.mechanism: The C14 phase behaves as a soft ferromagnet with a Curie temperature of 214 K, distinct from the high-coercivity behavior of the fcc phase.
item.system: C14 Laves phase in FeCoNiTi (and the C14-dominant alloy Fe27Co27Ni17Ti29)
item.supporting_observation: The C14-dominant alloy shows a single main ferromagnetic transition at 246 K (close to 214 K in the dual phase) and lacks the high coercivity seen in the fcc phase of the main alloy.
item.scope_limits: The C14 phase in the dual-phase alloy shows a transition at 214 K, while the C14-dominant alloy shows anomalies at 246 K and 183 K, suggesting microstructural or compositional variations affect the exact Tc.
item.alternatives_considered: The possibility of the C14 phase being paramagnetic or having a different magnetic order was ruled out by the sharp rise in susceptibility.
quotes: The C14 phase demonstrates the characteristics of a soft ferromagnet.
The increase of χdc below approximately 275 K signifies a FM ground state.
The C14 phase in FeCoNiTi governs the ferromagnetic ordering at 214 K.
